newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal Finmin plays down German comments on euro.
newsitem.headline: Portugal Finmin plays down German comments on euro.

text.p: Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco said he was confident Portugal would join the European single currency at its launch despite recent remarks by a German official that some countries were not ready to take part.

"(State Secretary at the German Finance Ministry) Juergen Stark, who is an important man in this process, made a speech aimed at markets in defence of the mark," Sousa Franco told a parliamentary commission on European affairs.
"This is a political game. German industrialists and others are very frightened of Italy joining (the euro)," he said.

Stark said last week that some countries should foresake the political prestige of joining the European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) from the outset in 1999 if their economic structures were not ready.
He did not name names but his comments appeared to be directed at so-called "Club Med" countries, including Portugal, which have not yet established a track record of exchange rate stability.
Sousa Franco said he thought Stark's remarks were aimed at Italy.
"This is a manoeuvre to neutralise internal German opposition, but it is the question of Italy that is up for discussion in 1997," he said.
"When they make these comments they are not thinking about Portugal at all, for reasons which are crystal clear. We have shown that we have (economic) sustainability," he said.
"We must have the sense to see that this is Italy's battle but that we are on the battlefield and we must defend ourselves."
He said Italy was making a big effort to meet the EMU criteria, adding: "Nothing will be achieved in Europe without Italy or against Italy."
Sousa Franco said that the recent volatility of the escudo, which has followed the peseta lower, was a slight upset but would have no impact on the downward trend in interest rates.
"Interest rates are tending to stabilise in Portugal but they could go down further," he said.
But the minister warned that currency and money markets could see increasing volatility in 1997 and 1998.
"When George Soros carries more weight than Helmut Kohl -- and Soros has already shown he weighs more than sterling -- then this is a very dangerous atmosphere," Sousa Franco said.

He was referring to the Hungarian-born financier who is credited with having almost single-handedly driven the British pound out of the Exchange Rate Mechanism in 1992. On Monday Soros said that markets need not panic if Italy and Spain missed the start of EMU. -- Lisbon editorial +(351-1) 3538254
